LESSON: WRITING 5.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTERS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.5: Writing 5.5.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letters
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.5.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letters, part of Strand 5 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do people write letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for parts of a letter of apology,

2. listen to two conversations: one that constitutes an apology and another that doesn’t, from a digital device,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for parts of a letter of apology,
2. listen to two conversations: one that constitutes an apology and another that doesn’t, from a digital device,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.5.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letters together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner completes the given task on time when writing letters of apology.

• Digital Literacy: It is developed as the learner interacts with digital devices to search for sample letters of apology from the

internet.

Values:
Unity: It is promoted as the learner collaborates in the writing of letters of apology.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peaceful conflict resolution: It is promoted as the learner practises apologising to peers and seniors.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the skill of writing letters of apology to the learning of functional writing in Kiswahili.
